gaps.text: In-line measurement of Powder temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor at the probe

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: one calibration per method first, then the synchronised NIR and Raman blocks concatenated into a single matrix with block scaling so that neither method dominates. Both probes must look at the same small powder volume in the feed frame; if they cannot share one window, the fused model is not meaningful. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out batches, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.)
Achievable detection limit and accuracy for API concentration in a powder blend - no source gives a figure for this kind of application.
The geometry and mounting of a probe in the customer's specific feed frame; the sources show a probe designed for a tablet-press feed frame, not for this press.

items.finding: Temperature sensitivity of the OH bands in NIR and MIR can be a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that temperature control or measurement may be important for NIR/MIR measurements, so consider monitoring temperature at the probe.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The quote concerns aqueous solution and tempered sample holders, not powder or an in-line probe; transfer to a powder feed frame is uncertain.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: The source explored low-level data fusion by concatenating preprocessed NIR and Raman spectra, and also evaluated mid-level data fusion using extracted features.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing low-level and mid-level fusion for NIR and Raman in a feed-frame application, while checking whether fusion improves performance over single methods.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Abstract only; the study used a specific formulation and instrument, and gives no geometry or mounting details for the customer's feed frame.

citation.quote: For model development and validation, low-level data fusion was explored through concatenation of preprocessed NIR and Raman spectra. Mid-level data fusion was also evaluated, based on extracted features of the preprocessed data.
citation.label: E04 ¶1

items.finding: Block scaling is often recommended for data fusion but can sometimes have a worse effect on results than other preprocessing methods.
items.how_it_applies: When planning block scaling for NIR/Raman fusion, test alternative preprocessing and validate whether scaling helps or harms the fused model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The quote is from a review context and is not specific to powder blends or NIR/Raman; no scale or in-line details are given.

citation.quote: While block scaling is often recommended for data fusion, sometimes it can have a worse effect on results than other pre-processing methods (17).
citation.label: E03 ¶16
